newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Products-Gasoline down on ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Products-Gasoline down on ample supplies.

text.p: Weekly inventory data helped pressure spot refined products prices lower Tuesday, while active gasoline deliveries and imports to New York Harbor kept differentials there on the defensive.

Data released by the Energy Information Agency of the Department of Energy, which was delayed until early afternoon, was less bearish than Tuesday evening's American Petroleum Institute (API) report, traders said, showing a more modest gasoline build of 900,000 barrels.

On Tuesday, API said gasoline output for the week ended May 30 stood at 8.195 million barrels a day, helping overall stocks jump 2.9 million barrels. The EIA put refinery output at a massive 100.4 percent of capacity, which should keep the spot markets well supplied.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline fell 1.02 cents by the settlement and July heating oil dipped 0.42 cents.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Gasoline differentials slipped in the New York Harbor Wednesday, weighed down by ample supply stoked by high refinery runs and steady cargoes.
"The Harbor is well supplied and reiterates the fact that we have high output and good imports," said a New York Harbor dealer.

Prompt regular conventional gasoline was offered at 2.00 cents under the July NYMEX gasoline contract versus 1.75 cents under Tuesday. Reformulated 87 grade was offered at 0.40 to 0.50 cent over the July contract versus 0.75 cent over Tuesday.
Reformulated premium 93 grade was offered at 8.00 cents over the July contract, falling from its offer of 9.00 to 9.25 cents over.
On Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said gasoline output for the week ended May 30 stood at 8.195 million barrels a day.

Dealers said a 1.0 to 1.5 million barrel delivery of reformulated gasoline British Petroleum is taking on the June NYMEX contract may begin to weigh on the market if they can not find any buyers for the fuel.

"I would not want to be taking such a large delivery of gasoline when there is so much supply in the Harbor," said a dealer. Traders said BP may have to underbid the market just to find buyers, but BP officials said they expected no problems finding buyers.

Little change was reported in heating oil with the contango between the NYMEX July and August heating oil contracts encouraging storage. Heating oil was offered at unchanged to the screen as was the case this morning when it fell from Sun Co's posting of 0.20 cent above the July NYMEX contract.
"Once the storage tanks are filled, that's when we may see weakness because the incentive to buy will not be there," said a Harbor dealer.
Morgan Stabnley was said to be taking a more than two million barrel delivery on the June heating oil contract to place in storage and resell in the winter when values usually firm.
CARGOES
Besides record gasoline output at refineries, a steady flow of gasoline continues to hit the U.S. as imports.

"The cargoes that are coming over are not extraordinary, but I expect gasoline cargoes to continue to come in a brisk pace and average 350,000 to 500,000 barrels a day this summer," said a New York Harbor dealer.
U.S. GULF COAST
Prompt conventional regular M1 gasoline remained steady, with traders reporting barrels changing hands at 1.60 cents under July NYMEX, near flat with late Monday levels.
Sellers raised offers slightly early in the day, though the lack of strong buying interest prevented any bullish movement.
"I didn't see anybody buying that didn't need barrels buying today. There wasn't a great rush to the market," one player said.
MIDCONTINENT

The Midcontinent unleaded gasoline markets were quiet late Wednesday after seeing sharp declines in the morning following bearish API data. Group Three unleaded differentials remained 3.50 to 3.90 cents over NYMEX July after being talked 0.75 cent lower Wednesday morning.
Chicago unleaded differentials also stayed largely steady at 3.25 to 3.75 cents. Activity was extremely light.
"We have had a very quiet week so far," said a Houston-based products trader. The low sulphur and jet fuel markets were also quiet.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
